461	    def export(self, dataset: str, version: int, destination: str | Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
462	        """Deliver the CSV and manifest for a version into *destination*.
463	
464	        The stored blob is snapshotted once as raw bytes and checked against
465	        the version record (existence, SHA-256, CSV structure per the import
466	        rules, record count, field set, and inferred types) before anything
467	        is written, so the delivered CSV always matches the selected version
468	        even if the stored file changes mid-export. Both output files are
469	        landed through temporary files with the previous contents backed up;
470	        any failure restores the destination directory to its prior state
471	        and leaves no new or temporary files behind. The workspace itself is
472	        only read, never modified.
473	        """
474	        state = self._load()
475	        record = self._version_record(state, dataset, version)
476	        # A corrupt catalog record is reported as inconsistent source data,
477	        # never as a KeyError/TypeError escaping the documented interface.
478	        self._verified_manifest_record(record)
479	        blob_name = record.get("blob")
480	        if not isinstance(blob_name, str) or not blob_name:
481	            raise ValueError(f"stored data record incomplete for {dataset}@{version}")
482	
483	        source = self.workspace / blob_name
484	        if not source.exists():
485	            raise ValueError(f"stored data missing for {dataset}@{version}")
486	        # Snapshot the source once as raw bytes: the hash check, the
487	        # structural parse, and the delivered CSV all derive from this same
488	        # read, so a concurrent rewrite of the blob cannot produce a
489	        # delivery that disagrees with the version record.
490	        with source.open("rb") as handle:
491	            content = handle.read()
492	        if hashlib.sha256(content).hexdigest() != record["content_sha256"]:
493	            raise ValueError(f"stored data hash mismatch for {dataset}@{version}")
494	        try:
495	            header, rows = _read_csv_records(content)
496	        except ValueError as error:
497	            raise ValueError(
498	                f"stored CSV for {dataset}@{version} is invalid: {error}"
499	            ) from error
500	
501	        # The snapshot must agree with everything the version record claims;
502	        # a mismatch means the stored data and the catalog have drifted apart.
503	        if len(rows) != record["row_count"]:
504	            raise ValueError(
505	                f"stored data record count mismatch for {dataset}@{version}: "
506	                f"the record lists {record['row_count']} but the data has {len(rows)}"
507	            )
508	        schema = record["schema"]
509	        if set(header) != set(schema):
510	            raise ValueError(
511	                f"stored data field set mismatch for {dataset}@{version}"
512	            )
513	        observed = {name: set() for name in header}
514	        for row in rows:
515	            for position, name in enumerate(header):
516	                observed[name].add(_kind(row[position]))
517	        inferred = {name: _merge_kinds(kinds) for name, kinds in observed.items()}
518	        if inferred != schema:
519	            raise ValueError(
520	                f"stored data type inference mismatch for {dataset}@{version}"
521	            )
522	
523	        data_name = f"{dataset}-v{version}.csv"
524	        manifest = {"schemaVersion": 1, "record": record, "file": data_name}
525	        if str(version) in state["lineage"].get(dataset, {}):
526	            # Cleaned versions carry their full lineage chain in the manifest.
527	            manifest["lineage"] = self.lineage(dataset, version)["chain"]
528	        manifest_bytes = (
529	            json.dumps(manifest, indent=2, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n"
530	        ).encode("utf-8")
531	
532	        # All checks passed before this point; only now is the destination
533	        # created or touched.
534	        destination_path = Path(destination).resolve()
535	        destination_path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
536	        if not destination_path.is_dir():
537	            raise OSError(f"export destination is not a directory: {destination_path}")
538	        data_path = destination_path / data_name
539	        manifest_path = destination_path / "manifest.json"
540	        self._deliver_export(
541	            destination_path,
542	            ((data_path, content), (manifest_path, manifest_bytes)),
543	        )
544	        return manifest

546	    @staticmethod
547	    def _deliver_export(
548	        directory: Path, outputs: tuple[tuple[Path, bytes], ...]
549	    ) -> None:
550	        """Atomically replace *outputs* inside *directory*, rolling back on failure.
551	
552	        Each pre-existing target is first renamed aside as a backup, then
553	        every new file is written to a temporary file in the same directory
554	        and renamed into place. Any failure removes the new files, restores
555	        the backups, and deletes temporary files, so the directory keeps
556	        exactly its prior contents; on success the backups are removed.
557	        """
558	        for target, _ in outputs:
559	            if target.is_dir() and not target.is_symlink():
560	                raise OSError(
561	                    f"cannot overwrite non-file export target: {target}"
562	                )
563	        backups: list[tuple[Path, Path]] = []
564	        placed: list[Path] = []
565	        try:
566	            for target, _ in outputs:
567	                if not target.exists() and not target.is_symlink():
568	                    continue
569	                descriptor, backup_name = tempfile.mkstemp(
570	                    prefix=f".{target.name}.", suffix=".bak", dir=directory
571	                )
572	                os.close(descriptor)
573	                backup = Path(backup_name)
574	                backup.unlink()
575	                os.replace(target, backup)
576	                backups.append((target, backup))
577	            for target, payload in outputs:
578	                descriptor, temporary_name = tempfile.mkstemp(
579	                    prefix=f".{target.name}.", suffix=".tmp", dir=directory
580	                )
581	                temporary = Path(temporary_name)
582	                try:
583	                    # mkstemp defaults to 0600; match the ordinary
584	                    # create-mode (0666 masked by the umask) of a plain copy.
585	                    umask = os.umask(0)
586	                    os.umask(umask)
587	                    os.fchmod(descriptor, 0o666 & ~umask)
588	                    with os.fdopen(descriptor, "wb") as handle:
589	                        handle.write(payload)
590	                        handle.flush()
591	                        os.fsync(handle.fileno())
592	                    temporary.replace(target)
593	                except BaseException:
594	                    with suppress(OSError):
595	                        temporary.unlink()
596	                    raise
597	                placed.append(target)
598	        except BaseException:
599	            for target in placed:
600	                with suppress(OSError):
601	                    target.unlink()
602	            for target, backup in reversed(backups):
603	                with suppress(OSError):
604	                    os.replace(backup, target)
605	            raise
606	        for _, backup in backups:
607	            with suppress(OSError):
608	                backup.unlink()

614	    @staticmethod
615	    def _verified_manifest_record(record: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
616	        """Validate the ``record`` object embedded in an export manifest."""
617	        if not isinstance(record, dict):
618	            raise ValueError("manifest record must be an object")
619	        dataset = record.get("dataset")
620	        if not isinstance(dataset, str) or not dataset:
621	            raise ValueError("manifest record.dataset must be a non-empty string")
622	        version = record.get("version")
623	        if not _is_int(version) or version < 1:
624	            raise ValueError("manifest record.version must be a positive integer")
625	        content_hash = record.get("content_sha256")
626	        if not _is_hash(content_hash):
627	            raise ValueError(
628	                "manifest record.content_sha256 must be 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters"
629	            )
630	        row_count = record.get("row_count")
631	        if not _is_int(row_count) or row_count < 0:
632	            raise ValueError("manifest record.row_count must be a non-negative integer")
633	        schema = record.get("schema")
634	        if not isinstance(schema, dict) or not schema:
635	            raise ValueError("manifest record.schema must be a non-empty object")
636	        for name, kind in schema.items():
637	            if not isinstance(name, str) or not name:
638	                raise ValueError("manifest record.schema field names must be non-empty strings")
639	            if not isinstance(kind, str) or kind not in _TYPE_NAMES:
640	                raise ValueError(
641	                    f"manifest record.schema declares an invalid type for field {name!r}"
642	                )
643	        return record

645	    @staticmethod
646	    def _verified_lineage_entry(entry: Any) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
647	        """Validate the linkage fields of one lineage chain entry."""
648	        if not isinstance(entry, dict):
649	            return None
650	        dataset = entry.get("dataset")
651	        if not isinstance(dataset, str) or not dataset:
652	            return None
653	        version = entry.get("version")
654	        if not _is_int(version) or version < 1:
655	            return None
656	        source_version = entry.get("sourceVersion")
657	        if not _is_int(source_version) or source_version < 1:
658	            return None
659	        if not _is_hash(entry.get("sourceSha256")) or not _is_hash(entry.get("contentSha256")):
660	            return None
661	        row_count = entry.get("rowCount")
662	        if not _is_int(row_count) or row_count < 0:
663	            return None
664	        return entry

666	    def _lineage_issues(
667	        self, chain: Any, record: dict[str, Any], issues: list[dict[str, str]]
668	    ) -> None:
669	        if not isinstance(chain, list):
670	            issues.append({"code": "lineage", "message": "lineage must be an array"})
671	            return
672	        entries: list[dict[str, Any] | None] = []
673	        for index, raw_entry in enumerate(chain):
674	            entry = self._verified_lineage_entry(raw_entry)
675	            if entry is None:
676	                issues.append(
677	                    {
678	                        "code": "lineage",
679	                        "message": f"lineage entry {index + 1} is missing required fields "
680	                        "or uses invalid field types",
681	                    }
682	                )
683	            entries.append(entry)
684	
685	        for index, entry in enumerate(entries):
686	            if entry is None:
687	                continue
688	            if entry["dataset"] != record["dataset"]:
689	                issues.append(
690	                    {
691	                        "code": "lineage",
692	                        "message": f"lineage entry {index + 1} belongs to dataset "
693	                        f"{entry['dataset']!r}, expected {record['dataset']!r}",
694	                    }
695	                )
696	            if entry["sourceVersion"] >= entry["version"]:
697	                issues.append(
698	                    {
699	                        "code": "lineage",
700	                        "message": f"lineage entry {index + 1} has source version "
701	                        f"{entry['sourceVersion']} that is not below version {entry['version']}",
702	                    }
703	                )
704	
705	        for index in range(1, len(entries)):
706	            previous, current = entries[index - 1], entries[index]
707	            if previous is None or current is None:
708	                continue
709	            if current["sourceVersion"] != previous["version"]:
710	                issues.append(
711	                    {
712	                        "code": "lineage",
713	                        "message": f"lineage entry {index + 1} continues version "
714	                        f"{current['sourceVersion']} but the previous entry is version "
715	                        f"{previous['version']}",
716	                    }
717	                )
718	            elif current["sourceSha256"] != previous["contentSha256"]:
719	                issues.append(
720	                    {
721	                        "code": "lineage",
722	                        "message": f"lineage entry {index + 1} source hash does not match "
723	                        "the content hash of the previous entry",
724	                    }
725	                )
726	
727	        if entries:
728	            last = entries[-1]
729	            if last is not None:
730	                if last["version"] != record["version"]:
731	                    issues.append(
732	                        {
733	                            "code": "lineage",
734	                            "message": f"last lineage entry is version {last['version']} but "
735	                            f"the record is version {record['version']}",
736	                        }
737	                    )
738	                if last["contentSha256"] != record["content_sha256"]:
739	                    issues.append(
740	                        {
741	                            "code": "lineage",
742	                            "message": "last lineage entry content hash does not match the "
743	                            "record hash",
744	                        }
745	                    )
746	                if last["rowCount"] != record["row_count"]:
747	                    issues.append(
748	                        {
749	                            "code": "lineage",
750	                            "message": f"last lineage entry reports {last['rowCount']} records "
751	                            f"but the record reports {record['row_count']}",
752	                        }
753	                    )

755	    def verify_export(self, directory: str | Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
756	        """Verify an exported directory offline against its manifest.
757	
758	        Only ``manifest.json`` and the CSV it names inside *directory* are
759	        read; no workspace state is consulted and nothing is written.
760	        Manifest or parameter problems raise ValueError, read failures
761	        OSError. Data discrepancies are returned as issue objects grouped
762	        by code: missing, hash, csv, rows, schema, lineage.
763	        """
764	        manifest_path = Path(directory) / "manifest.json"
765	        try:
766	            manifest_text = manifest_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
767	        except UnicodeDecodeError as error:
768	            raise ValueError(f"manifest is not valid UTF-8: {error}") from error
769	        try:
770	            manifest = json.loads(manifest_text)
771	        except json.JSONDecodeError as error:
772	            raise ValueError(f"manifest is not valid JSON: {error}") from error
773	
774	        if not isinstance(manifest, dict):
775	            raise ValueError("manifest must be a JSON object")
776	        schema_version = manifest.get("schemaVersion")
777	        if not _is_int(schema_version) or schema_version != 1:
778	            raise ValueError("manifest schemaVersion must be the integer 1")
779	        if "record" not in manifest:
780	            raise ValueError("manifest is missing required field: record")
781	        if "file" not in manifest:
782	            raise ValueError("manifest is missing required field: file")
783	        record = self._verified_manifest_record(manifest["record"])
784	        file_name = manifest["file"]
785	        if (
786	            not isinstance(file_name, str)
787	            or not file_name
788	            or file_name in (".", "..")
789	            or "/" in file_name
790	            or "\\" in file_name
791	            or "\0" in file_name
792	        ):
793	            raise ValueError(
794	                "manifest file must be a non-empty file name without path separators"
795	            )
796	
797	        # Resolve purely lexically (no target content is read) and refuse
798	        # anything that escapes the export directory, including via links.
799	        base = Path(directory).resolve()
800	        try:
801	            resolved = (base / file_name).resolve(strict=False)
802	        except (OSError, RuntimeError):
803	            # Python 3.12 reports a symlink loop as RuntimeError. The
804	            # underlying message embeds a machine path and is intentionally
805	            # not surfaced.
806	            raise ValueError(
807	                f"manifest file {file_name!r} could not be safely resolved "
808	                "(broken or looping reference)"
809	            )
810	        if resolved != base and base not in resolved.parents:
811	            raise ValueError(
812	                f"manifest file {file_name!r} resolves outside the export directory"
813	            )
814	
815	        issues: list[dict[str, str]] = []
816	        lineage = manifest.get("lineage")
817	        if lineage is not None:
818	            # Missing or null lineage means no chain was shipped; an empty
819	            # array is likewise a chain-free (legacy) export.
820	            self._lineage_issues(lineage, record, issues)
821	
822	        if not resolved.exists():
823	            issues.append(
824	                {
825	                    "code": "missing",
826	                    "message": f"data file {file_name!r} listed in the manifest is missing",
827	                }
828	            )
829	        else:
830	            data = resolved.read_bytes()
831	            content_hash = hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
832	            if content_hash != record["content_sha256"]:
833	                issues.append(
834	                    {
835	                        "code": "hash",
836	                        "message": "CSV content hash does not match the manifest record",
837	                    }
838	                )
839	
840	            header: list[str] | None = None
841	            rows: list[list[str]] = []
842	            header_ok = False
843	            records_ok = False
844	            can_parse = True
845	            try:
846	                text = data.decode("utf-8")
847	            except UnicodeDecodeError as error:
848	                issues.append(
849	                    {"code": "csv", "message": f"CSV is not valid UTF-8: {error.reason}"}
850	                )
851	                text = ""
852	                can_parse = False
853	            if can_parse and _ends_inside_quote(text):
854	                issues.append(
855	                    {"code": "csv", "message": "CSV has a quoted field that is never closed"}
856	                )
857	                can_parse = False
858	            if can_parse:
859	                parse_failed = False
860	                try:
861	                    # Non-strict parsing matches import semantics: only the
862	                    # explicitly enumerated structural problems are failures.
863	                    parsed = [
864	                        row
865	                        for row in csv.reader(io.StringIO(text, newline=""))
866	                        if row != []
867	                    ]
868	                except csv.Error as error:
869	                    issues.append(
870	                        {"code": "csv", "message": f"CSV structure is invalid: {error}"}
871	                    )
872	                    parsed = []
873	                    parse_failed = True
874	                if not parsed and not parse_failed:
875	                    issues.append({"code": "csv", "message": "CSV has no header row"})
876	                elif parsed:
877	                    header = parsed[0]
878	                    rows = parsed[1:]
879	                    empty_positions = [
880	                        position + 1 for position, name in enumerate(header) if name == ""
881	                    ]
882	                    if empty_positions:
883	                        issues.append(
884	                            {
885	                                "code": "csv",
886	                                "message": "CSV header has empty field name(s) at "
887	                                f"position(s) {empty_positions}",
888	                            }
889	                        )
890	                    seen: set[str] = set()
891	                    duplicates: list[str] = []
892	                    for name in header:
893	                        if name in seen and name not in duplicates:
894	                            duplicates.append(name)
895	                        seen.add(name)
896	                    if duplicates:
897	                        issues.append(
898	                            {
899	                                "code": "csv",
900	                                "message": "CSV header has duplicate field name(s): "
901	                                + ", ".join(repr(name) for name in duplicates),
902	                            }
903	                        )
904	                    header_ok = not empty_positions and not duplicates
905	                    ragged = [
906	                        row_number
907	                        for row_number, row in enumerate(rows, start=1)
908	                        if len(row) != len(header)
909	                    ]
910	                    if ragged:
911	                        issues.append(
912	                            {
913	                                "code": "csv",
914	                                "message": f"CSV record(s) {ragged} do not have the same "
915	                                f"number of fields as the header ({len(header)})",
916	                            }
917	                        )
918	                    records_ok = header_ok and not ragged
919	
920	            if header is not None:
921	                # Record numbering ignores blank physical lines and quoted
922	                # newlines already, so the count stays determinable even when
923	                # individual records are ragged.
924	                if len(rows) != record["row_count"]:
925	                    issues.append(
926	                        {
927	                            "code": "rows",
928	                            "message": f"CSV contains {len(rows)} data record(s) but the "
929	                            f"manifest record lists {record['row_count']}",
930	                        }
931	                    )
932	
933	            if header_ok:
934	                # The field set is fixed by the header and stays checkable
935	                # even when some data records are ragged.
936	                assert header is not None
937	                expected_schema = record["schema"]
938	                actual_fields = set(header)
939	                missing_fields = sorted(name for name in expected_schema if name not in actual_fields)
940	                extra_fields = sorted(name for name in actual_fields if name not in expected_schema)
941	                if missing_fields or extra_fields:
942	                    details = []
943	                    if missing_fields:
944	                        details.append("missing from CSV: " + ", ".join(missing_fields))
945	                    if extra_fields:
946	                        details.append("unexpected in CSV: " + ", ".join(extra_fields))
947	                    issues.append(
948	                        {
949	                            "code": "schema",
950	                            "message": "CSV field set does not match the manifest record ("
951	                            + "; ".join(details)
952	                            + ")",
953	                        }
954	                    )
955	                if records_ok:
956	                    # Type inference needs consistent column counts so each
957	                    # value can be aligned with its header position.
958	                    observed = {name: set() for name in header}
959	                    for row in rows:
960	                        for position, name in enumerate(header):
961	                            observed[name].add(_kind(row[position]))
962	                    inferred = {
963	                        name: _merge_kinds(kinds) for name, kinds in observed.items()
964	                    }
965	                    for name in sorted(expected_schema):
966	                        if name in inferred and inferred[name] != expected_schema[name]:
967	                            issues.append(
968	                                {
969	                                    "code": "schema",
970	                                    "message": f"field {name!r} infers as {inferred[name]!r} "
971	                                    f"but the manifest record declares "
972	                                    f"{expected_schema[name]!r}",
973	                                }
974	                            )
975	
976	        category_order = {
977	            "missing": 0,
978	            "hash": 1,
979	            "csv": 2,
980	            "rows": 3,
981	            "schema": 4,
982	            "lineage": 5,
983	        }
984	        issues.sort(key=lambda issue: category_order[issue["code"]])
985	        return {
986	            "dataset": record["dataset"],
987	            "version": record["version"],
988	            "passed": not issues,
989	            "issues": issues,
990	        }

992	    @staticmethod
993	    def _column_array(value: Any, where: str) -> list[str]:
994	        if not isinstance(value, list) or not value:
995	            raise ValueError(f"{where} must be a non-empty array")
996	        if any(not isinstance(name, str) or not name for name in value):
997	            raise ValueError(f"{where} must contain only non-empty strings")
998	        if len(set(value)) != len(value):
999	            raise ValueError(f"{where} must not contain duplicates")
1000	        return list(value)

1002	    @classmethod
1003	    def _validate_reference_payload(cls, rule: dict[str, Any], where: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
1004	        misplaced = set(rule) - _REFERENCE_RULE_KEYS
1005	        if misplaced:
1006	            raise ValueError(f"{where} has unknown attributes: {sorted(misplaced)}")
1007	        columns = cls._column_array(rule.get("columns"), f"{where}.columns")
1008	        reference = rule.get("reference")
1009	        if not isinstance(reference, dict):
1010	            raise ValueError(f"{where}.reference must be an object")
1011	        extra = set(reference) - _REFERENCE_KEYS
1012	        if extra:
1013	            raise ValueError(f"{where}.reference has unknown attributes: {sorted(extra)}")
1014	        dataset = reference.get("dataset")
1015	        if not isinstance(dataset, str) or not dataset:
1016	            raise ValueError(f"{where}.reference.dataset must be a non-empty string")
1017	        version = reference.get("version")
1018	        if not _is_int(version) or version < 1:
1019	            raise ValueError(f"{where}.reference.version must be a positive integer")
1020	        ref_columns = cls._column_array(
1021	            reference.get("columns"), f"{where}.reference.columns"
1022	        )
1023	        if len(columns) != len(ref_columns):
1024	            raise ValueError(
1025	                f"{where}.columns and {where}.reference.columns must have the same length"
1026	            )
1027	        return {
1028	            "id": rule["id"],
1029	            "type": "reference",
1030	            "columns": columns,
1031	            "reference": {
1032	                "dataset": dataset,
1033	                "version": version,
1034	                "columns": ref_columns,
1035	            },
1036	        }
1037	
1038	    @classmethod
1039	    def _validate_rules_payload(cls, rules: Any) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
1040	        if not isinstance(rules, list) or not rules:
1041	            raise ValueError("rules must be a non-empty array")
1042	        normalized: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
1043	        seen_ids: set[str] = set()
1044	        for index, rule in enumerate(rules):
1045	            where = f"rules[{index}]"
1046	            if not isinstance(rule, dict):
1047	                raise ValueError(f"{where} must be an object")
1048	            extra = set(rule) - _RULE_KEYS
1049	            if extra:
1050	                raise ValueError(f"{where} has unknown attributes: {sorted(extra)}")
1051	            identifier = rule.get("id")
1052	            if not isinstance(identifier, str) or not identifier:
1053	                raise ValueError(f"{where}.id must be a non-empty string")
1054	            if identifier in seen_ids:
1055	                raise ValueError(f"duplicate rule id: {identifier}")
1056	            rule_type = rule.get("type")
1057	            if rule_type not in _RULE_TYPES:
1058	                raise ValueError(f"{where}.type must be one of {sorted(_RULE_TYPES)}")
1059	            if rule_type == "reference":
1060	                normalized.append(cls._validate_reference_payload(rule, where))
1061	                seen_ids.add(identifier)
1062	                continue
1063	            misplaced = set(rule) & {"columns", "reference"}
1064	            if misplaced:
1065	                raise ValueError(f"{where} has unknown attributes: {sorted(misplaced)}")
1066	            column = rule.get("column")

1397	    def _validate_with_references(
1398	        self,
1399	        state: dict[str, Any],
1400	        dataset: str,

1408	        strings — no trimming, no numeric conversion, and separators inside
1409	        values have no special meaning. Empty values or duplicate complete
1410	        combinations on a reference side fail the whole run, even when the
1411	        local side has no records.

1414	            state, dataset, version, rules
1415	        )
1416	
1417	        # Build each referenced combination set before scanning local rows,
1418	        # so reference-side problems surface even with zero local records.
1419	        combination_sets: dict[str, set[tuple[str, ...]]] = {}
1420	        for rule in rules:
1421	            if rule["type"] != "reference":
1422	                continue
1423	            reference = rule["reference"]
1424	            key = (reference["dataset"], reference["version"])
1425	            _, ref_header, ref_rows = references[key]
1426	            positions = [ref_header.index(name) for name in reference["columns"]]
1427	            combinations: set[tuple[str, ...]] = set()
1428	            for record_number, row in enumerate(ref_rows, start=1):
1429	                combination = tuple(row[position] for position in positions)
1430	                if any(part == "" for part in combination):
1431	                    raise ValueError(
1432	                        f"empty value in referenced column(s) of "
1433	                        f"{reference['dataset']}@{reference['version']} "
1434	                        f"record {record_number}"
1435	                    )
1436	                if combination in combinations:
1437	                    raise ValueError(
1438	                        f"duplicate complete combination in referenced "
1439	                        f"{reference['dataset']}@{reference['version']}"
1440	                    )
1441	                combinations.add(combination)
1442	            combination_sets[rule["id"]] = combinations
1443	
1444	        column_positions = {
1445	            rule["id"]: [
1446	                header.index(name)
1447	                for name in (
1448	                    rule["columns"] if rule["type"] == "reference" else [rule["column"]]
1449	                )
1450	            ]
1451	            for rule in rules
1452	        }
1453	        violations_by_id: dict[str, list[int]] = {rule["id"]: [] for rule in rules}

1556	    @staticmethod
1557	    def _validate_operations_payload(operations: Any) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
1558	        if not isinstance(operations, list) or not operations:
1559	            raise ValueError("operations must be a non-empty array")
1560	        normalized: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
1561	        for index, operation in enumerate(operations):
1562	            where = f"operations[{index}]"
1563	            if not isinstance(operation, dict):
1564	                raise ValueError(f"{where} must be an object")
1565	            operation_type = operation.get("type")
1566	            if operation_type not in _OPERATION_KEYS:
1567	                raise ValueError(f"{where}.type must be one of {sorted(_OPERATION_KEYS)}")
1568	            expected = _OPERATION_KEYS[operation_type]
1569	            if set(operation) != expected:
1570	                raise ValueError(f"{where} must have exactly the attributes {sorted(expected)}")
1571	            if operation_type in ("trim", "rename"):
1572	                if not isinstance(operation["column"], str) or not operation["column"]:
1573	                    raise ValueError(f"{where}.column must be a non-empty string")
1574	            if operation_type == "rename":
1575	                if not isinstance(operation["to"], str) or not operation["to"]:
1576	                    raise ValueError(f"{where}.to must be a non-empty string")
1577	            if operation_type == "drop_duplicates":
1578	                columns = operation["columns"]
1579	                if not isinstance(columns, list) or not columns:
1580	                    raise ValueError(f"{where}.columns must be a non-empty array")
1581	                if any(not isinstance(name, str) or not name for name in columns):
1582	                    raise ValueError(f"{where}.columns must contain only non-empty strings")
1583	                if len(set(columns)) != len(columns):
1584	                    raise ValueError(f"{where}.columns must not contain duplicates")
1585	            normalized.append(dict(operation))
1586	        return normalized

1590	        with blob_path.open("r", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as handle:
1591	            # Blank physical lines are not data records, matching DictReader.
1592	            parsed = [row for row in csv.reader(handle) if row != []]
1593	        if not parsed:
1594	            raise ValueError(f"stored CSV for {dataset}@{version} has no header")
1595	        header = parsed[0]
1596	        if any(name == "" for name in header):

1610	    def clean(self, dataset: str, version: int, operations: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
1611	        """Clean a stored version and append the result as a new immutable version.
1612	
1613	        ``operations`` is a parsed non-empty JSON array, or a path to a file
1614	        containing one. Any failure (unknown dataset/version, missing or
1615	        tampered blob, unreadable or invalid operations, malformed stored CSV,
1616	        write failure) leaves the catalog untouched and consumes no version
1617	        number.
1618	        """
1619	        if isinstance(operations, (str, Path)):
1620	            with open(operations, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
1621	                operations = json.load(handle)
1622	        steps_plan = self._validate_operations_payload(operations)
1623	
1624	        state = self._load()
1625	        record = self._version_record(state, dataset, version)
1626	        blob_path = self.workspace / record["blob"]
1627	        if not blob_path.exists():
1628	            raise ValueError(f"stored data missing for {dataset}@{version}")
1629	        source_hash = _sha256(blob_path)
1630	        if source_hash != record["content_sha256"]:
1631	            raise ValueError(f"stored data hash mismatch for {dataset}@{version}")
1632	
1633	        header, rows = self._read_stored_csv(blob_path, dataset, version)
1634	
1635	        columns = list(header)
1636	        origins = list(header)  # source column behind each current column
1637	        sources = list(range(1, len(rows) + 1))  # 1-based source record numbers
1638	        steps: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
1639	        for operation in steps_plan:
1640	            operation_type = operation["type"]
1641	            step: dict[str, Any] = {"operation": dict(operation), "inputRows": len(rows)}
1642	            if operation_type == "trim":
1643	                column = operation["column"]
1644	                if column not in columns:
1645	                    raise ValueError(f"unknown column {column!r} for trim")
1646	                position = columns.index(column)
1647	                modified = []
1648	                for index, row in enumerate(rows):
1649	                    stripped = row[position].strip()
1650	                    if stripped != row[position]:
1651	                        row[position] = stripped
1652	                        modified.append(sources[index])
1653	                step["modifiedRows"] = modified
1654	            elif operation_type == "rename":
1655	                column = operation["column"]
1656	                target = operation["to"]
1657	                if column not in columns:
1658	                    raise ValueError(f"unknown column {column!r} for rename")
1659	                if target in columns:
1660	                    raise ValueError(f"rename target {target!r} conflicts with an existing column")
1661	                columns[columns.index(column)] = target
1662	                step["from"] = column
1663	                step["to"] = target
1664	            else:
1665	                selected = operation["columns"]
1666	                for name in selected:
1667	                    if name not in columns:
1668	                        raise ValueError(f"unknown column {name!r} for drop_duplicates")
1669	                positions = [columns.index(name) for name in selected]
1670	                seen: set[tuple[str, ...]] = set()
1671	                kept_rows: list[list[str]] = []
1672	                kept_sources: list[int] = []
1673	                deleted = []
1674	                for row, source in zip(rows, sources):
1675	                    key = tuple(row[position] for position in positions)
1676	                    if key in seen:
1677	                        deleted.append(source)
1678	                    else:
1679	                        seen.add(key)
1680	                        kept_rows.append(row)
1681	                        kept_sources.append(source)
1682	                rows, sources = kept_rows, kept_sources
1683	                step["deletedRows"] = deleted
1684	            step["outputRows"] = len(rows)
1685	            steps.append(step)
1686	
1687	        # Deterministic serialization: identical source and operations always
1688	        # produce identical CSV bytes.
1689	        buffer = io.StringIO()
1690	        writer = csv.writer(buffer, lineterminator="\n")
1691	        writer.writerow(columns)
1692	        writer.writerows(rows)
1693	        content = buffer.getvalue().encode("utf-8")
1694	        content_hash = hashlib.sha256(content).hexdigest()
1695	        # The result blob is stored with the same integrity rules as an
1696	        # import: an existing file is reused only after its bytes verify
1697	        # against the result hash, and a new file lands atomically so a
1698	        # write failure leaves no partial blob behind. Any failure here
1699	        # happens before the version and lineage are appended, so no version
1700	        # number is consumed.
1701	        blob = self._store_blob(content, content_hash)
1702	
1703	        observed = {name: set() for name in columns}
1704	        for row in rows:
1705	            for position, name in enumerate(columns):
1706	                observed[name].add(_kind(row[position]))
1707	
1708	        versions = state["datasets"][dataset]
1709	        new_version = len(versions) + 1
1710	        new_record = DatasetVersion(
1711	            dataset=dataset,
1712	            version=new_version,
1713	            source_name=f"{dataset}-v{new_version}-cleaned.csv",
1714	            content_sha256=content_hash,
1715	            row_count=len(rows),
1716	            schema={name: _merge_kinds(kinds) for name, kinds in observed.items()},
1717	            imported_at=datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
1718	            blob=str(blob.relative_to(self.workspace)),
1719	        )
1720	        entry = {
1721	            "dataset": dataset,
1722	            "version": new_version,
1723	            "sourceVersion": version,
1724	            "sourceSha256": source_hash,
1725	            "operations": steps_plan,
1726	            "steps": steps,
1727	            "columnMapping": {name: origins[index] for index, name in enumerate(columns)},
1728	            "rowMapping": list(sources),
1729	            "rowCount": len(rows),
1730	            "contentSha256": content_hash,
1731	        }
1732	        # Version and lineage are persisted in a single save; a write failure
1733	        # leaves no version, no lineage record, and no consumed version number.
1734	        versions.append(asdict(new_record))
1735	        state["lineage"].setdefault(dataset, {})[str(new_version)] = entry
1736	        self._save(state)
1737	        result = asdict(new_record)
1738	        result["lineage"] = entry
1739	        return result

1741	    def lineage(self, dataset: str, version: int) -> dict[str, Any]:
1742	        """Return the full cleaning chain for a version, source-first.
1743	
1744	        Plain imported versions are chain starts and yield an empty chain.
1745	        """
1746	        state = self._load()
1747	        self._version_record(state, dataset, version)
1748	        records = state["lineage"].get(dataset, {})
1749	        chain: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
1750	        current = version
1751	        while str(current) in records:
1752	            entry = records[str(current)]
1753	            chain.append(json.loads(json.dumps(entry)))
1754	            current = entry["sourceVersion"]
1755	        chain.reverse()
1756	        return {"dataset": dataset, "version": version, "chain": chain}

import csv as csv_module
import hashlib
import io
import json
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path
from unittest import mock

from governance_workbench import Catalog
from governance_workbench.catalog import _read_csv_records

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]


def legacy_import(catalog: Catalog, dataset: str, contents: str) -> str:
    """Simulate a version stored by a pre-strictness build.

    Writes the bytes directly to the content-addressed blob directory and
    appends a catalog record using the old, permissive inference rules, so
    tests can exercise how downstream stages handle legacy ragged data
    without going through the now-strict importer.
    """
    import csv as csv_module
    import hashlib

    from governance_workbench.catalog import _kind, _merge_kinds

    data = contents.encode("utf-8")
    content_hash = hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
    catalog.blobs.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    blob = catalog.blobs / f"{content_hash}.csv"
    blob.write_bytes(data)

    reader = csv_module.DictReader(io.StringIO(contents, newline=""))
    fieldnames = reader.fieldnames or []
    observed = {name: set() for name in fieldnames}
    row_count = 0
    for row in reader:
        row_count += 1
        for name in fieldnames:
            observed[name].add(_kind(row[name] or ""))

    state = catalog._load()
    versions = state["datasets"].setdefault(dataset, [])
    versions.append(
        {
            "dataset": dataset,
            "version": len(versions) + 1,
            "source_name": "legacy.csv",
            "content_sha256": content_hash,
            "row_count": row_count,
            "schema": {name: _merge_kinds(kinds) for name, kinds in observed.items()},
            "imported_at": "2000-01-01T00:00:00+00:00",
            "blob": str(blob.relative_to(catalog.workspace)),
        }
    )
    catalog._save(state)
    return content_hash


class CatalogTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.temporary = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.root = Path(self.temporary.name)
        self.catalog = Catalog(self.root / "workspace")

    def tearDown(self):
        self.temporary.cleanup()

    def csv(self, name: str, contents: str) -> Path:
        path = self.root / name
        path.write_text(contents, encoding="utf-8")
        return path

    def test_import_infers_schema_and_preserves_blob(self):
        source = self.csv("input.csv", "id,active,score\n1,true,2.5\n2,false,3\n")
        record = self.catalog.import_csv("metrics", source)
        source.write_text("changed", encoding="utf-8")
        self.assertEqual(record.schema, {"id": "integer", "active": "boolean", "score": "number"})
        self.assertEqual(record.row_count, 2)
        self.assertNotEqual((self.catalog.workspace / record.blob).read_text(), "changed")

    def test_compare_reports_schema_and_row_changes(self):
        self.catalog.import_csv("people", self.csv("one.csv", "id,name\n1,Ada\n"))
        self.catalog.import_csv("people", self.csv("two.csv", "id,name,region\n1,Ada,EU\n2,Lin,APAC\n"))
        result = self.catalog.compare("people", 1, 2)
        self.assertEqual(result["addedFields"], ["region"])
        self.assertEqual(result["rowDelta"], 1)
        self.assertTrue(result["contentChanged"])

    def test_export_manifest_matches_stored_content(self):
        record = self.catalog.import_csv("events", self.csv("events.csv", "id\n1\n"))
        destination = self.root / "export"
        manifest = self.catalog.export("events", 1, destination)
        on_disk = json.loads((destination / "manifest.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        self.assertEqual(on_disk, manifest)
        self.assertEqual(manifest["record"]["content_sha256"], record.content_sha256)


class StrictImportTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.temporary = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.root = Path(self.temporary.name)
        self.catalog = Catalog(self.root / "workspace")

    def tearDown(self):
        self.temporary.cleanup()

    def write(self, contents, name: str = "data.csv") -> Path:
        path = self.root / name
        if isinstance(contents, bytes):
            path.write_bytes(contents)
        else:
            path.write_text(contents, encoding="utf-8")
        return path

    def reject(self, contents):
        path = self.write(contents)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as context:
            self.catalog.import_csv("d", path)
        return str(context.exception)

    # ---- validity rules with distinct reasons ----------------------------

    def test_invalid_files_rejected_with_distinct_reasons(self):
        cases = {
            "no header (empty file)": "",
            "empty header field": "a,\n1,2\n",
            "duplicate header field": "a,a\n1,2\n",
            "record too short": "a,b\n1\n",
            "record too long": "a,b\n1,2,3\n",
            "unclosed quote": 'a,b\n1,"unclosed\n',
        }
        messages = set()
        for label, contents in cases.items():
            message = self.reject(contents)
            self.assertTrue(message, label)
            self.assertNotIn(str(self.root), message)
            messages.add(message)
        self.assertEqual(len(messages), len(cases))

        # invalid UTF-8
        path = self.write(b"a,b\n1,\xff\n")
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as context:
            self.catalog.import_csv("d", path)
        self.assertIn("UTF-8", str(context.exception))
        messages.add(str(context.exception))

        # parse error: a field over the reader's size limit is a csv.Error
        path = self.write("a\n" + ("x" * 100) + "\n")
        previous_limit = csv_module.field_size_limit()
        try:
            csv_module.field_size_limit(10)
            with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as context:
                self.catalog.import_csv("d", path)
        finally:
            csv_module.field_size_limit(previous_limit)
        self.assertIn("could not be parsed", str(context.exception))

    def test_field_count_error_names_record_number_actual_and_expected(self):
        # blank physical lines are skipped; the quoted newline stays in record 1,
        # so the ragged line is data record 2
        path = self.write('a,b\n\n1,"line one\nline two"\n2,3,4\n')
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as context:
            self.catalog.import_csv("d", path)
        message = str(context.exception)
        self.assertIn("data record 2", message)
        self.assertIn("3 field(s)", message)
        self.assertIn("expected 2", message)

        # a short record reports its own number and actual count
        path = self.write("a,b,c\n1,2,3\n4\n")
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as context:
            self.catalog.import_csv("d", path)
        message = str(context.exception)
        self.assertIn("data record 2", message)
        self.assertIn("1 field(s)", message)
        self.assertIn("expected 3", message)

    # ---- accepted shapes --------------------------------------------------

    def test_header_only_file_imports_with_zero_rows_and_null_types(self):
        record = self.catalog.import_csv("d", self.write("a,b\n"))
        self.assertEqual(record.row_count, 0)
        self.assertEqual(record.schema, {"a": "null", "b": "null"})
        rows = self.catalog.list_datasets()["d"]
        self.assertEqual(len(rows), 1)

    def test_blank_lines_and_quoted_newlines_match_record_semantics(self):
        contents = 'id,name\n\n1,"line one\nline two"\n\n2,Bob\n'
        record = self.catalog.import_csv("d", self.write(contents))
        self.assertEqual(record.row_count, 2)

    def test_empty_vs_whitespace_inference_and_quote_then_text_kept(self):
        record = self.catalog.import_csv(
            "d", self.write("id,v,w\n1,,s\n2, ,\"x\"y\n")
        )
        # "" is missing/null, " " is a whitespace string; "x"y parses as xy
        self.assertEqual(record.schema, {"id": "integer", "v": "string", "w": "string"})
        _, rows = _read_csv_records((self.catalog.workspace / record.blob).read_bytes())
        self.assertEqual(rows[0][1], "")
        self.assertEqual(rows[1][1], " ")
        self.assertEqual(rows[1][2], "xy")

    def test_stored_bytes_match_source_exactly(self):
        contents = 'id,name\r\n1, "Ada" \r\n2,"line one\nline two"\r\n'
        source = self.write(contents)
        record = self.catalog.import_csv("d", source)
        stored = (self.catalog.workspace / record.blob).read_bytes()
        # newlines, spacing and quoting are preserved byte-for-byte
        self.assertEqual(stored, contents.encode("utf-8"))
        self.assertEqual(record.content_sha256, hashlib.sha256(stored).hexdigest())

    def test_later_source_change_does_not_affect_version(self):
        source = self.write("id,v\n1,5\n")
        record = self.catalog.import_csv("d", source)
        source.write_text("id,v\n9,999\n", encoding="utf-8")
        reloaded = Catalog(self.catalog.workspace)
        stored = (reloaded.workspace / record.blob).read_bytes()
        self.assertEqual(stored, b"id,v\n1,5\n")
        self.assertEqual(reloaded.get("d", 1)["content_sha256"], record.content_sha256)

    def test_source_replaced_during_import_cannot_desynchronize_version(self):
        # The file on disk (B, ragged) differs from the bytes the importer
        # snapshots at read time (A). The stored blob and record must both
        # describe A; the old code re-read the path while copying and ended
        # up storing B under A's description.
        valid = b"id,v\n1,5\n"
        source = self.write(b"id,v\n1,5,extra\n")
        real_open = Path.open

        def snapshot_open(path, *args, **kwargs):
            if Path(path) == source:
                return io.BytesIO(valid)
            return real_open(path, *args, **kwargs)

        with mock.patch.object(Path, "open", snapshot_open):
            record = self.catalog.import_csv("d", source)
        stored = (self.catalog.workspace / record.blob).read_bytes()
        self.assertEqual(stored, valid)
        self.assertEqual(record.content_sha256, hashlib.sha256(valid).hexdigest())
        export_dir = self.root / "out"
        self.catalog.export("d", 1, export_dir)
        self.assertTrue(Catalog(self.root / "offline").verify_export(export_dir)["passed"])

    # ---- content-addressed storage ---------------------------------------

    def test_repeated_imports_append_versions_but_share_blob(self):
        source = self.write("id,v\n1,5\n")
        first = self.catalog.import_csv("d", source)
        second = self.catalog.import_csv("d", source)
        third = self.catalog.import_csv("d", source)
        self.assertEqual([r["version"] for r in self.catalog.list_datasets()["d"]], [1, 2, 3])
        self.assertEqual({first.blob, second.blob, third.blob}, {first.blob})
        self.assertEqual(
            first.content_sha256,
            self.catalog.get("d", 3)["content_sha256"],
        )

    def test_existing_matching_blob_is_reused(self):
        data = b"id,v\n1,5\n"
        content_hash = hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
        self.catalog.blobs.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        existing = self.catalog.blobs / f"{content_hash}.csv"
        existing.write_bytes(data)
        record = self.catalog.import_csv("d", self.write(data.decode("utf-8")))
        self.assertEqual(record.blob, str(existing.relative_to(self.catalog.workspace)))
        self.assertEqual(existing.read_bytes(), data)

    def test_corrupt_existing_blob_errors_and_is_not_overwritten(self):
        data = b"id,v\n1,5\n"
        content_hash = hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
        self.catalog.blobs.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        damaged = self.catalog.blobs / f"{content_hash}.csv"
        damaged.write_bytes(b"id,v\n9,9\n")
        with self.assertRaises(OSError):
            self.catalog.import_csv("d", self.write(data.decode("utf-8")))
        # the corrupt file is untouched and no version appeared
        self.assertEqual(damaged.read_bytes(), b"id,v\n9,9\n")
        self.assertEqual(self.catalog.list_datasets(), {})
        # once storage is repaired, reuse succeeds
        damaged.write_bytes(data)
        record = self.catalog.import_csv("d", self.write(data.decode("utf-8")))
        self.assertEqual(record.version, 1)
        self.assertEqual(record.content_sha256, content_hash)

    # ---- failure atomicity ------------------------------------------------

    def test_invalid_data_creates_nothing_and_consumes_no_version(self):
        self.reject("a,b\n1,2,3\n")
        self.assertFalse(self.catalog.state_path.exists())
        self.assertEqual(self.catalog.list_datasets(), {})
        # no stray temporary files in the blob directory
        leftovers = list(self.catalog.blobs.glob("*.tmp")) if self.catalog.blobs.exists() else []
        self.assertEqual(leftovers, [])
        # retry uses the original next version number
        record = self.catalog.import_csv("d", self.write("a,b\n1,2\n", "good.csv"))
        self.assertEqual(record.version, 1)

    def test_failed_import_after_good_version_consumes_no_version(self):
        self.catalog.import_csv("d", self.write("a,b\n1,2\n", "v1.csv"))
        self.reject("a,b\n1,2,3\n")
        record = self.catalog.import_csv("d", self.write("a,b\n3,4\n", "v2.csv"))
        self.assertEqual(record.version, 2)
        self.assertEqual(len(self.catalog.list_datasets()["d"]), 2)

    def test_blob_write_failure_leaves_no_blob_and_no_version(self):
        with mock.patch.object(tempfile, "mkstemp", side_effect=OSError("disk full")):
            with self.assertRaises(OSError):
                self.catalog.import_csv("d", self.write("a,b\n1,2\n"))
        self.assertFalse(self.catalog.state_path.exists())
        self.assertEqual(list(self.catalog.blobs.iterdir()), [])
        record = self.catalog.import_csv("d", self.write("a,b\n1,2\n"))
        self.assertEqual(record.version, 1)

    def test_state_write_failure_leaves_no_version_but_blob_remains(self):
        with mock.patch.object(Catalog, "_save", side_effect=OSError("disk full")):
            with self.assertRaises(OSError):
                self.catalog.import_csv("d", self.write("a,b\n1,2\n"))
        self.assertEqual(self.catalog.list_datasets(), {})
        # the orphaned blob is content-addressed and verified on reuse
        record = self.catalog.import_csv("d", self.write("a,b\n1,2\n"))
        self.assertEqual(record.version, 1)

    def test_missing_and_unreadable_source_raise_oserror(self):
        with self.assertRaises(OSError):
            self.catalog.import_csv("d", self.root / "missing.csv")
        source = self.write("a,b\n1,2\n")
        real_open = Path.open

        def deny_open(path, *args, **kwargs):
            if Path(path) == source:
                raise PermissionError("denied")
            return real_open(path, *args, **kwargs)

        with mock.patch.object(Path, "open", deny_open):
            with self.assertRaises(OSError):
                self.catalog.import_csv("d", source)
        self.assertEqual(self.catalog.list_datasets(), {})

    def test_failed_import_invisible_after_restart(self):
        self.reject("a,b\n1,2,3\n")
        reloaded = Catalog(self.catalog.workspace)
        self.assertEqual(reloaded.list_datasets(), {})

    # ---- round trip --------------------------------------------------------

    def test_imported_version_exports_and_verifies(self):
        contents = 'id,name\n1,"Ada"\n2,"Bo\nby"\n'
        self.catalog.import_csv("d", self.write(contents))
        export_dir = self.root / "out"
        self.catalog.export("d", 1, export_dir)
        report = Catalog(self.root / "offline").verify_export(export_dir)
        self.assertTrue(report["passed"], report["issues"])


class RulesConfigurationTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.temporary = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.root = Path(self.temporary.name)
        self.catalog = Catalog(self.root / "workspace")
        source = self.root / "things.csv"
        source.write_text("id,v\n1,5\n", encoding="utf-8")
        self.catalog.import_csv("things", source)

    def tearDown(self):
        self.temporary.cleanup()

    def test_valid_rule_shapes(self):
        result = self.catalog.set_rules(
            "things",
            [
                {"id": "r1", "column": "id", "type": "required"},
                {"id": "r2", "column": "id", "type": "unique"},
                {"id": "r3", "column": "v", "type": "range", "min": 0},
                {"id": "r4", "column": "v", "type": "range", "max": 10},
                {"id": "r5", "column": "v", "type": "range", "min": -1.5, "max": 10.5},
            ],
        )
        self.assertEqual(result["revision"], 1)
        self.assertEqual([rule["id"] for rule in result["rules"]], ["r1", "r2", "r3", "r4", "r5"])

    def test_revisions_are_contiguous_and_immutable(self):
        first = self.catalog.set_rules("things", [{"id": "a", "column": "id", "type": "required"}])
        second = self.catalog.set_rules("things", [{"id": "b", "column": "v", "type": "unique"}])
        self.assertEqual((first["revision"], second["revision"]), (1, 2))
        state = json.loads(self.catalog.state_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        self.assertEqual(state["rules"]["things"][0]["rules"][0]["id"], "a")
        self.assertEqual(state["rules"]["things"][1]["rules"][0]["id"], "b")

    def test_unknown_dataset_rejected(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.catalog.set_rules("missing", [{"id": "a", "column": "id", "type": "required"}])

    def test_invalid_configurations(self):
        def reject(rules):
            with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                self.catalog.set_rules("things", rules)

        reject([])
        reject("not-a-list")
        reject([None])
        reject(["not-an-object"])
        reject([{"column": "id", "type": "required"}])  # missing id
        reject([{"id": "", "column": "id", "type": "required"}])  # empty id
        reject([{"id": 5, "column": "id", "type": "required"}])  # non-string id
        reject([{"id": "a"}])  # missing column and type
        reject([{"id": "a", "column": "", "type": "required"}])  # empty column
        reject([{"id": "a", "column": 7, "type": "required"}])
        reject([{"id": "a", "column": "id", "type": "mystery"}])  # unknown type
        reject(
            [
                {"id": "a", "column": "id", "type": "required"},
                {"id": "a", "column": "v", "type": "unique"},  # duplicate id
            ]
        )
        reject([{"id": "a", "column": "id", "type": "required", "extra": 1}])
        reject([{"id": "a", "column": "v", "type": "range"}])  # no bounds
        reject([{"id": "a", "column": "v", "type": "range", "min": 10, "max": 1}])
        reject([{"id": "a", "column": "v", "type": "range", "min": True}])
        reject([{"id": "a", "column": "v", "type": "range", "max": False}])
        reject([{"id": "a", "column": "v", "type": "range", "min": "1"}])
        reject([{"id": "a", "column": "v", "type": "range", "min": float("nan")}])
        reject([{"id": "a", "column": "v", "type": "range", "max": float("inf")}])
        reject([{"id": "a", "column": "id", "type": "required", "min": 1}])
        reject([{"id": "a", "column": "id", "type": "unique", "max": 1}])

    def test_failed_write_does_not_consume_revision_and_retry_succeeds(self):
        with mock.patch.object(Catalog, "_save", side_effect=OSError("disk full")):
            with self.assertRaises(OSError):
                self.catalog.set_rules("things", [{"id": "a", "column": "id", "type": "required"}])
        state = json.loads(self.catalog.state_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        self.assertEqual(state.get("rules", {}).get("things", []), [])
        result = self.catalog.set_rules("things", [{"id": "a", "column": "id", "type": "required"}])
        self.assertEqual(result["revision"], 1)

    def test_works_with_legacy_workspace_state(self):
        state_path = self.catalog.state_path
        state = json.loads(state_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        del state["rules"]
        del state["validations"]
        state_path.write_text(json.dumps(state), encoding="utf-8")
        result = self.catalog.set_rules("things", [{"id": "a", "column": "id", "type": "required"}])
        self.assertEqual(result["revision"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(self.catalog.validate("things", 1)["passed"], True)


class ValidationTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.temporary = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.root = Path(self.temporary.name)
        self.catalog = Catalog(self.root / "workspace")

    def tearDown(self):
        self.temporary.cleanup()

    def csv_file(self, contents: str, name: str = "data.csv") -> Path:
        path = self.root / name
        path.write_text(contents, encoding="utf-8")
        return path

    def test_required_unique_range_semantics(self):
        csv_contents = (
            "id,v,label\n"
            "1,0,a\n"          # row 1: in range, unique values so far
            "2,10,a\n"         # row 2: boundary max included; duplicate label
            "3,-1,b\n"         # row 3: below min
            "4,11, c\n"        # row 4: above max
            "5,,\n"            # row 5: missing v skipped by range, missing label
            "6,abc,d\n"        # row 6: non-numeric
            "7,true,e\n"       # row 7: boolean-looking cell is not a number
            "8,inf,f\n"        # row 8: non-finite
            "9,nan,g\n"        # row 9: non-finite
            "10, 5,h\n"        # row 10: whitespace is not stripped
            "11,5.0,i\n"       # row 11: finite numeric passes
            "12,1e1,j\n"       # row 12: 10.0 passes (max inclusive)
            " ,0,k\n"          # row 13: whitespace id is present and distinct
        )
        self.catalog.import_csv("things", self.csv_file(csv_contents))
        self.catalog.set_rules(
            "things",
            [
                {"id": "id-required", "column": "id", "type": "required"},
                {"id": "label-unique", "column": "label", "type": "unique"},
                {"id": "v-range", "column": "v", "type": "range", "min": 0, "max": 10},
            ],
        )
        report = self.catalog.validate("things", 1)
        by_id = {item["id"]: item for item in report["results"]}
        self.assertEqual([item["id"] for item in report["results"]],
                         ["id-required", "label-unique", "v-range"])
        self.assertEqual(by_id["id-required"]["violations"], [])
        self.assertEqual(by_id["label-unique"]["violations"], [1, 2])
        self.assertEqual(by_id["v-range"]["violations"], [3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10])
        self.assertEqual(by_id["v-range"]["violationCount"], 7)
        self.assertFalse(report["passed"])
        self.assertEqual(report["rowCount"], 13)
        self.assertTrue(all(
            item["violations"] == sorted(item["violations"])
            for item in report["results"]
        ))

    def test_quoted_newline_does_not_advance_row_number(self):
        csv_contents = "id,name\n1,\"line one\nline two\"\n2,\n"
        self.catalog.import_csv("notes", self.csv_file(csv_contents))
        self.catalog.set_rules(
            "notes",
            [
                {"id": "name-required", "column": "name", "type": "required"},
                {"id": "name-unique", "column": "name", "type": "unique"},
            ],
        )
        report = self.catalog.validate("notes", 1)
        by_id = {item["id"]: item for item in report["results"]}
        self.assertEqual(report["rowCount"], 2)
        self.assertEqual(by_id["name-required"]["violations"], [2])
        self.assertEqual(by_id["name-unique"]["violations"], [])

    def test_empty_string_missing_but_whitespace_present(self):
        self.catalog.import_csv("ws", self.csv_file("id,v\n1,\n2, \n3,  \n"))
        self.catalog.set_rules("ws", [{"id": "req", "column": "v", "type": "required"}])
        report = self.catalog.validate("ws", 1)
        self.assertEqual(report["results"][0]["violations"], [1])
        self.assertEqual(report["rowCount"], 3)

    def test_unique_reports_whole_duplicate_group_raw_strings(self):
        self.catalog.import_csv("u", self.csv_file("v\nx\nx\ny\nx\n z\nz\n"))
        self.catalog.set_rules("u", [{"id": "u1", "column": "v", "type": "unique"}])
        report = self.catalog.validate("u", 1)
        # rows 1,2,4 share "x"; " z" and "z" are distinct raw strings
        self.assertEqual(report["results"][0]["violations"], [1, 2, 4])

    def test_range_min_only_and_max_only_endpoints(self):
        self.catalog.import_csv("r", self.csv_file("v\n0\n5\n10\n"))
        self.catalog.set_rules(
            "r",
            [
                {"id": "lo", "column": "v", "type": "range", "min": 0},
                {"id": "hi", "column": "v", "type": "range", "max": 10},
            ],
        )
        report = self.catalog.validate("r", 1)
        self.assertTrue(report["passed"])

    def test_columns_match_verbatim(self):
        self.catalog.import_csv("c", self.csv_file(" id\n1\n"))
        self.catalog.set_rules("c", [{"id": "r", "column": "id", "type": "required"}])
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.catalog.validate("c", 1)

    def test_missing_data_version_revision_and_rules(self):
        self.catalog.import_csv("d", self.csv_file("v\n1\n"))
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.catalog.validate("d", 1)  # no rules
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.catalog.validate("missing", 1)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.catalog.validate("d", 2)
        self.catalog.set_rules("d", [{"id": "r", "column": "v", "type": "required"}])

        # tamper with the stored blob: repeated validation must notice

        (self.catalog.workspace / record["blob"]).write_text("v\n999\n", encoding="utf-8")
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):

        self.catalog.set_rules("d", [{"id": "r", "column": "v", "type": "required"}])
        record = self.catalog.get("d", 1)

        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):

    def test_history_persists_across_restart_in_revision_order(self):
        self.catalog.import_csv("d", self.csv_file("v\n1\n"))
        self.assertEqual(self.catalog.validation_history("d", 1), [])
        self.catalog.set_rules("d", [{"id": "r", "column": "v", "type": "required"}])
        self.catalog.set_rules("d", [{"id": "r", "column": "v", "type": "unique"}])
        self.catalog.validate("d", 1, revision=1)
        self.catalog.validate("d", 1, revision=2)
        reloaded = Catalog(self.catalog.workspace)
        history = reloaded.validation_history("d", 1)
        self.assertEqual([item["rulesRevision"] for item in history], [1, 2])
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            reloaded.validation_history("d", 99)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            reloaded.validation_history("missing", 1)

    def test_failed_report_write_leaves_no_partial_result(self):
        self.catalog.import_csv("d", self.csv_file("v\n1\n"))
        self.catalog.set_rules("d", [{"id": "r", "column": "v", "type": "required"}])
        with mock.patch.object(Catalog, "_save", side_effect=OSError("disk full")):
            with self.assertRaises(OSError):
                self.catalog.validate("d", 1)
        self.assertEqual(self.catalog.validation_history("d", 1), [])
        report = self.catalog.validate("d", 1)
        self.assertTrue(report["passed"])
        self.assertEqual(len(self.catalog.validation_history("d", 1)), 1)

    def test_validate_does_not_modify_data_or_add_versions(self):

    def test_invalid_reference_configurations(self):
        self.import_reference_side()
        self.catalog.import_csv("orders", self.csv_file("客户号,地区\nC1,北\n", "orders.csv"))

        def reject(rule):
            with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                self.catalog.set_rules("orders", [rule])

        reject({"id": "r", "type": "reference",
                "reference": {"dataset": "客户", "version": 2, "columns": ["编号"]}})  # no columns
        reject(self.reference_rule(reference=None))  # missing reference object
        reject(self.reference_rule(extra=1))  # extra attribute
        reject(self.reference_rule(column="客户号"))  # single-column form not allowed
        reject(self.reference_rule(min=1))
        reject(self.reference_rule(max=2))
        reject(self.reference_rule(columns=[]))  # empty columns
        reject(self.reference_rule(columns="客户号"))  # not an array
        reject(self.reference_rule(columns=["客户号", ""]))  # empty name
        reject(self.reference_rule(columns=["客户号", 7]))  # non-string
        reject(self.reference_rule(columns=["客户号", "客户号"]))  # duplicates
        reject(self.reference_rule(reference={"dataset": "客户", "version": 2,
                                              "columns": ["编号", "地区"], "x": 1}))
        reject(self.reference_rule(reference={"version": 2, "columns": ["编号", "地区"]}))
        reject(self.reference_rule(reference={"dataset": "", "version": 2,
                                              "columns": ["编号", "地区"]}))
        reject(self.reference_rule(reference={"dataset": 5, "version": 2,
                                              "columns": ["编号", "地区"]}))
        reject(self.reference_rule(reference={"dataset": "客户",
                                              "columns": ["编号", "地区"]}))  # no version
        reject(self.reference_rule(reference={"dataset": "客户", "version": 0,
                                              "columns": ["编号", "地区"]}))
        reject(self.reference_rule(reference={"dataset": "客户", "version": -1,
                                              "columns": ["编号", "地区"]}))
        reject(self.reference_rule(reference={"dataset": "客户", "version": True,
                                              "columns": ["编号", "地区"]}))
        reject(self.reference_rule(reference={"dataset": "客户", "version": 2.0,
                                              "columns": ["编号", "地区"]}))
        reject(self.reference_rule(reference={"dataset": "客户", "version": 2,
                                              "columns": []}))
        reject(self.reference_rule(reference={"dataset": "客户", "version": 2,
                                              "columns": ["编号", "编号"]}))
        reject(self.reference_rule(reference={"dataset": "客户", "version": 2,
                                              "columns": ["编号"]}))  # unequal lengths
        reject(self.reference_rule(columns=["客户号"],
                                   reference={"dataset": "客户", "version": 2,
                                              "columns": ["编号", "地区"]}))
        # old rule types reject the new attributes
        reject({"id": "r", "column": "客户号", "type": "required", "columns": ["客户号"]})
        reject({"id": "r", "column": "客户号", "type": "unique",
                "reference": {"dataset": "客户", "version": 2, "columns": ["编号"]}})
        # id uniqueness still applies across mixed types
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.catalog.set_rules(
                "orders",
                [
                    self.reference_rule(),
                    {"id": "客户引用", "column": "地区", "type": "required"},
                ],
            )

    def test_report_persists_and_revalidation_rechecks_every_side(self):
        self.import_reference_side()
        self.catalog.import_csv("orders", self.csv_file("客户号,地区\nC1,北\nC9,北\n", "orders.csv"))
        self.catalog.set_rules("orders", [self.reference_rule()])
        first = self.catalog.validate("orders", 1)
        second = self.catalog.validate("orders", 1)
        self.assertEqual(first, second)
        # exactly one report persisted, retrievable after a restart
        reloaded = Catalog(self.catalog.workspace)
        history = reloaded.validation_history("orders", 1)
        self.assertEqual(history, [first])
        state = json.loads(self.catalog.state_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        self.assertEqual(len(state["validations"]["orders"]["1"]), 1)

        # tampering with the reference side is noticed on revalidation
        reference_record = self.catalog.get("客户", 2)
        reference_blob = self.catalog.workspace / reference_record["blob"]
        reference_original = reference_blob.read_bytes()
        reference_blob.write_text("编号,地区,备注\nC1,北,x\n", encoding="utf-8")
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as context:
            reloaded.validate("orders", 1)
        self.assertIn("客户@2", str(context.exception))
        reference_blob.write_bytes(reference_original)

        # tampering with the local side is noticed as well
        local_record = self.catalog.get("orders", 1)
        local_blob = self.catalog.workspace / local_record["blob"]
        local_original = local_blob.read_bytes()
        local_blob.write_text("客户号,地区\nC1,北\n", encoding="utf-8")
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as context:
            reloaded.validate("orders", 1)
        self.assertIn("orders@1", str(context.exception))
        local_blob.write_bytes(local_original)

        # a missing reference file fails the run without touching the report
        reference_blob.unlink()
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as context:
            reloaded.validate("orders", 1)
        self.assertIn("客户@2", str(context.exception))
        reference_blob.write_bytes(reference_original)
        # the stored report survived every failed revalidation unchanged
        self.assertEqual(reloaded.validation_history("orders", 1), [first])
        self.assertEqual(reloaded.validate("orders", 1), first)
